thread.title: 2 Lucky 'Lottery' Winners Will Get a San Ramon Home For Under $300k - NewsBreak
thread.title_full: 2 Lucky 'Lottery' Winners Will Get a San Ramon Home For Under $300k - NewsBreak

author: Thomas Smith
title: 2 Lucky 'Lottery' Winners Will Get a San Ramon Home For Under $300k - NewsBreak
text:
8 hours ago Amenities at Iron Horse Village Photo by Lennar Two households will have a chance to buy a new San Ramon home for a price that sounds almost unbelievable: $241,407.
The homes are part of the city's Below Market Rate Home Ownership Program at Lennar's Iron Horse Village development. Each has two bedrooms, 2.5 bathrooms and approximately 1,187 square feet, according to the City of San Ramon's housing program page . They are located at 3029 Bolster Loop and 2005 Bolster Loop.
But there's an important timing detail: The deadline to enter the lottery was Tuesday, October 6, at 5 p.m. Anyone just learning about the opportunity has missed the published entry deadline.
A chance to buy, with conditions The "lottery" is an affordable housing opportunity drawing, rather than a giveaway. Selected buyers still have to qualify and purchase the homes.
The units are designated for eligible low-income households with two to five people. Solar is included in the purchase price, and the listing shows an HOA charge of $434.45.
Buyers also must accept a 30-year deed restriction. HouseKeys explains that the program requires owner occupancy and places restrictions on future resale. The discounted price comes with continuing obligations.
According to HouseKeys' Iron Horse Village listing , ranking results are expected to be published around the evening of October 14. The file submission deadline is October 22 at 5 p.m. Those dates are subject to change.
Applicants should understand that a favorable lottery number does not automatically mean they will get a home. HouseKeys verifies claimed preferences and eligibility, and final rankings can change during that review.
More affordable homes are coming Iron Horse Village is a 117-home development with a mix of single-family and multifamily residences, landscape paths, a private tot lot and a connection to the adjacent Iron Horse Trail.
The city is not offering down payment assistance for these purchases.
For people who missed this drawing, there is another reason to pay attention: These two homes are the first of six below-market-rate units planned for Iron Horse Village, according to the city's October 1 announcement .
The city's housing page lists the other four units with prices and drawing dates still to be determined. They include another two-bedroom home, two three-bedroom homes and a four-bedroom home, serving different income categories.
For now, existing applicants have paperwork and ranking results ahead of them. Everyone else can watch for the next opportunity.
